findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates the limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains for 29 minutes. A second request with the same device ID hits the cache and returns nil, so Authenticate grants anonymous access despite the limit. Concurrent requests can bypass the check the same way. Cache a device only after successful admission, and add a test that retries a rejected device.

findings.title: Device admission is not atomic with the limit check
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and performs the insert in another, without serializing admission. If the count is one below deviceLimit, multiple requests for distinct new devices can all observe the available slot and then insert successfully. All of those devices subsequently qualify for updates, so the configured limit can remain exceeded. Make the count-and-admit operation atomic across requests and Grafana instances, and test concurrent admission.

findings.title: Omitting the device header bypasses limit enforcement
findings.body: Authenticate relies on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny anonymous access, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Because this header is supplied by the client, an anonymous caller can omit it and continue accessing protected APIs even when the configured device limit is full; those requests are neither counted nor checked. Limit enforcement needs a defined admission path for requests without a device ID rather than treating missing identification as successful admission.
